newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean copper pipe market seen moving to surplus.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean copper pipe market seen moving to surplus.

text.p: South Korea's copper pipe and tube market is seen moving into oversupply in 1997 as domestic production capacity is expected to expand by 40,000 tonnes this year, traders and industry analysts said on Thursday.

"We are worried that there will be a surplus in the domestic market in 1997 as the local copper pipe industry has completed its plan to expand production capacity by 40,000 tonnes to 160,000 tonnes," said an official with the Korea Copper Industrial Cooperative. He added that South Korea's copper pipe capacity was 120,000 tonnes in 1995.
"The industry has expanded its production capacity without considering demand," the official said.
The sales price for copper pipe in the local market has tumbled to 2,600 won a kg currently, from 3,200 won in June.
Producers' inventories of copper pipe have doubled since June due to lagging demand stemming from the slowdown in the construction sector, the cooperative official said.
Copper pipe and tubes are used in the manufacture of air conditioners, refrigerators, water pipes and in the electronics industry generally.
"Local producers currently have copper pipe stocks equal to 30 days' requirements compared with 15 days in June," the official said.
The recent sharp depreciation of the won against the U.S. dollar had also squeezed domestic demand, he added.
Several small and medium-sized pipe firms have criticised LG Metals Corp for expanding its production capacity despite the oversupply in the local market.
Traders said that LG is aiming to capitalise on its cost advantages over its competitors, given by its own copper smelter operation, to expand its metal fabrication business.
A spokesman for LG Metals said it had started to expand its copper pipe capacity to reach 28,000 tonnes a year by the end of 1997 from its present capcity of 10,000 tonnes.
He said LG Metals would invest 22 billion won in its copper pipe plant in Seocheon on the west coast of South Korea.

"The roll margin (costs plus profit) for pipe production has already fallen by between 40 percent to 50 percent this year from 1.2 million won a tonne in 1995," a source at Poongsan Corp, South Korea's largest copper fabricator, said.
Traders said that while roll margins were now around 600,000 won a tonne, there were reports of sales done at margins as low as 400,000 won a tonne.
The Poongsan source said a breakeven roll margin would be around 800,000 won a tonne.
Poongsan is the third largest copper fabricator in the world and its sales of fabricted non-ferrous products totalled 181,459 tonnes in 1995, compared with 163,512 tonnes in 1994.
The company produced 82,187 tonnes of sheet and strip, 35,087 tonnes of pipe and tube, 22,196 tonnes of bar and rod, 18,595 tonnes of coin-blank and 23,394 tonnes of other products last year.
South Korea's demand for copper pipe is expected to rise to 135,000 tonnes this year from 111,000 tonnes in 1995, a trade ministry official said.
The offical said South Korea's pipe production is also expected to increase to 120,000 tonnes in 1996 from 99,000 tonnes a year earlier.
Pipe imports are forecast to rise to 15,000 tonnes this year from 12,000 tonnes in 1995, with exports seen up at 10,000 tonnes from 6,000 tonnes in 1995, he said.
-- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5651
